title: Contraction collapse order: shortest zero arc first, then survivor-inward per cluster, instead of most-contended-first (botijo spends 610k of 759k splits in its first 500 collapses)
description:
Experiment agreed with the user 2026-09-26. The contraction (NetworkContraction, LCBK19 Section 6.1) picks the next zero arc to collapse with ZeroArcCollapseOperator.mostContendedArc(): the collapsible zero arc whose movable node carries the most arcs, "so crowded fans clear while the mesh is still coarse". The paper prescribes no order (A.3 only proves termination), so the order is purely a cost choice, and the measured cost says the current one is the worst possible.

THE MEASUREMENT (master 9f5a5fce, default curvature bias -1, one quad-layout scene, 10 s per model; splits = working-copy vertices when the recarve starts minus when the contraction starts):

| model | arcs embedded | arcs after | splits | worst route | contract |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bolt | 334 | 84 | 921 | 2 | 0.18 s |
| hand | 3547 | 1360 | 23186 | 455 | 0.55 s |
| fertility | 3602 | 508 | 57011 | 2490 | 0.81 s |
| rockerarm | 1572 | 402 | 37420 | 1860 | 0.93 s |
| elk | 5546 | 1056 | 223171 | 12339 | 3.16 s |
| botijo | 6932 | 946 | 761700 | 169851 | 4.70 s |
| block, buddha, fandisk, feline | over 10 s | | | | |

Botijo's [contract] progress lines show where the cost goes: 610360 of 759389 splits, including the single 169851-split route, happen in the FIRST 500 of 3000 collapses; the remaining 2500 cost about 60 splits each. The first 500 are, by construction of mostContendedArc, the biggest fans, dragged while every arc is still claimed and free space around each node is at its minimum. Each dragged fan arc has to thread beside the still-claimed zero arc (kept as a wall until the last drag) for the wall's whole length, so the cost of one collapse is roughly (fan size) x (zero arc length in copy edges) x (lanes crossed), and along a chain of zero arcs the far arcs are dragged again at every step with routes that cumulate.

WHY THE COST IS OURS TO FIX: LCBK19 never times the re-embedding ("easily resolved by refinement with a few edge splits"), LCK21a times only the motorcycle graph and the ILP, and metriko (the MPL reference implementation, /home/acw/metriko) has no collapse code at all: its QGP example feeds the quantization straight into the integer-grid-map solve, and its README says the Lyon 2021 scheme is "currently under implementation". So there is no reference cost; the paper's paragraph has to be made cheap here.

THE TWO ORDERINGS TO TRY, in this order, each measured on its own:
1. Shortest zero arc first, measured in working-copy edges (the arc's ArcEdgePath length), among the collapsible zero arcs. Threading beside a one-edge wall costs about one split per fan arc; beside a twenty-edge wall, twenty. Zero arcs also grow when their nodes move (their path is re-routed with the node), so short ones should go before they lengthen. Lengths change during the contraction, so the choice must re-read them (a priority queue keyed on current length, or a rescan; the operator already keeps a compacted candidate list).
2. Survivor-inward within a cluster, with shortest-first as the tie-break. A connected cluster of zero arcs (union-find over zero arcs; LayoutExtraction already computes these clusters after quantization) ends at one node: the critical node when it has one (Def 6.2: critical nodes never move; A.3 case 1: at most one per cluster), otherwise a chosen member (prefer a node already on a mesh vertex, else the lowest id). Collapse only zero arcs adjacent to the current survivor, moving the other end onto it, so the survivor grows outward and every non-zero arc is re-routed exactly once. Leaf-first (what most-contended tends to do at cluster edges) re-routes the far arcs at every step of the chain with cumulating route lengths. Direction must still satisfy Def 6.2 (the moving node non-critical), which survivor-inward guarantees when the survivor is the critical node.

Keep master's most-contended order runnable during the experiment for the comparison, but do not land a knob: no system property, no run-scene flag, no new node input. The diff that lands makes the winning order the only order and records the others' numbers on the ticket.

CORRECTNESS EXPECTATION: the contracted layout is a fixed point the paper proves order-independent combinatorially, so the final '[recarve] nodes= arcs= patches=' counts must match master for every model that loads; only the embedding geometry and the split counts may differ. A changed count is a bug in the ordering code, not a result.

RELATED: PATCH-119 (merge zero-arc clusters before the embedding; its step 1 is measured and does not help, its worktree is left as is), PATCH-118 (block at bias -1, arc 178 fold-back, fix in REVIEW; block's result under the new order is worth recording), PATCH-111 (landed: the plain-Dijkstra rewrite of the collapse this ticket orders).
definition-of-done:
1. Baseline confirmed on the worktree before any change: the sweep table above reproduces (tmp/split_sweep.sh, 10 s per model, sphere_random never loaded).
2. Ordering 1 (shortest zero arc first, in copy edges, re-read as lengths change) implemented and swept; its table is on the ticket next to master's.
3. Ordering 2 (survivor-inward per cluster, shortest tie-break) implemented on top and swept; its table is on the ticket.
4. For every model that loads on master within 10 s (bolt, hand, fertility, rockerarm, elk, botijo), the final '[recarve] nodes= arcs= patches=' counts and the seamless metrics are unchanged under both orderings. Block, buddha, fandisk and feline are run under a 60 s cap with the winning order and their outcome recorded (loaded, failed with the message, or timed out).
5. The landed diff has one ordering, the better of the two by total splits on botijo and elk, with no knob; the ticket records why. If neither beats master, nothing lands and the ticket records the numbers and the reason.
6. Unit tests on a small hand-authored arrangement: (a) a chain of three zero arcs with a critical node at one end collapses survivor-inward, each non-zero arc re-routed once; (b) among two collapsible zero arcs the shorter (in copy edges) is chosen; (c) a zero arc that lengthened after a move is re-ranked.
7. No debugging scaffolding lands (wt done's diagnostics check).
testing-plan:
1. Baseline: `timeout 580 bash tmp/split_sweep.sh $PWD baseline > tmp/sweep-baseline.txt 2>&1` from the worktree; compare with tmp/sweep-master-baseline/ (master 9f5a5fce). Also record botijo's per-500-collapse [contract] progress lines as the shape to beat (610k of 759k splits in the first 500).
2. Implement ordering 1; sweep as `order1`; record the table and botijo's progress lines.
3. Implement ordering 2 on top; sweep as `order2`; record.
4. Under the winning order: block, buddha, fandisk, feline each alone under `timeout 60`; record outcomes.
5. Unit tests of DoD 6 and the full `mvn test`.
6. `ixd wt launch-add patch-120 --scene quad-layout` for botijo, a screenshot under tmp/, `ixd wt done patch-120`.
unknowns: Does survivor-inward need the whole cluster known up front (union-find before the first collapse), or is 'a zero arc with one end on a node that has already absorbed a collapse or is critical' an equivalent local rule?
When a cluster has no critical node, does the survivor choice change the split count materially, and is 'node already on a mesh vertex' the right preference?

Step C order2 (survivor-inward per zero-arc cluster, union-find over live zero arcs every pick; survivor = critical node, else a node with vertexId >= 0, else lowest id; only arcs whose non-survivor end may move per Def 6.2 qualify, shortest in copy edges among them; fallback to plain shortest when none qualifies, which happened only on the terminal empty pick of each round; tmp/sweep-order2.txt). splits / worst / contract s, order2 (order1 in brackets): bolt 529/0/0.15 (362); hand 8761/21/1.23 (7104); fertility 16759/59/0.82 (9214); rockerarm 6643/45/0.63 (3808); elk 26797/49/1.97 (11743); botijo 42009/142/2.57 (20120; the scene then ran past 10 s in the grid map under load average ~11, but its recarve line was reached); block loads, 31393/69/0.94 (11602). Botijo progress under order2: 607, 2506, 5856, 10565, 19475, 34522 at 500..3000 collapses, worst route 142. Recarve nodes/arcs/patches and seamless metrics identical to baseline for every model that loaded (botijo's recarve identical too). Order2 is worse than order1 on every model, about 2x on botijo and elk.

Step D correctness (tmp/correctness.sh over the sweep run logs, compared per model with the baseline): recarve nodes/arcs/patches and the [seamless] Metrics line are identical to baseline under order1 and under order2 for bolt, hand, fertility, rockerarm fig 8 and fig 9, elk and botijo; no count changed. Survivor-choice probe for unknown 2: EmbeddedNode.vertexId is never set on ArcNetwork nodes (always -1), so 'node already on a mesh vertex' was first a no-op; re-run with copyVertex < topology.originalVertexBound as the test (tmp/sweep-order2-meshvertex.txt) against lowest-id only (tmp/sweep-order2-lowid.txt): botijo 41971 vs 42009, elk 26751 vs 26797, hand 8766 vs 8761, rockerarm 6678 vs 6643, fertility 16759 both, bolt 534 vs 529: the survivor choice moves splits by under 1%. Order1 wins on botijo (20120 vs 42009) and elk (11743 vs 26797) and lands; order2 is removed. The landed code (method renamed ZeroArcCollapseOperator.shortestZeroArc, no switch) re-swept as tmp/sweep-landed.txt reproduces order1's split counts exactly.

Step E heavy models, landed shortest-first order, each alone under 60 s: block LOADS in 4.3 s (contract 0.93 s, 11602 splits, worst route 19, recarve nodes=154 arcs=316 patches=158); on master (worktree baseline and tmp/sweep-master-baseline) it failed in 2.8 s with 'the re-carved arrangement leaves a region of 3 faces ... bounded by arcs [178] that matches no live patch', the PATCH-118 fold-back, which does not occur under the new order. buddha LOADS in 37.0 s (contract 3.0 s, 18424 splits vs 36254 on master's partial 10 s run, worst 26 vs 176; recarve nodes=2500 arcs=4996 patches=2498, identical to master's; 19.7 s of the 37 s is the global grid map). feline LOADS in 22.3 s (contract 2.1 s, 23147 splits, worst 33, recarve nodes=1724 arcs=3452 patches=1726; seamless reports flippedTriangleCount=1 upstream of the contraction). fandisk FAILS in 0.6-2 s identically on master and here, in the embedding before the contraction starts: 'arc 815 runs exactly through copy vertex 684 (an original mesh vertex), which node -1 / arc 200 already holds'. Note: split_sweep.sh prints 'timeout' for any non-zero ixdar-cli model exit, so fandisk's and block's master 'timeout' rows were really these failures.

Step F: ZeroArcCollapseOperator.mostContendedArc is replaced by shortestZeroArc (fewest copy edges among collapsible live zero arcs, rescanned each pick, ties lowest arc id; no switch, no property); callers renamed (NetworkContraction.applyCollapse, EmbeddedTMeshScene, 9 unit tests). New unit test ixdar-app/test/unit/mesh/ZeroArcCollapseOrderTest on hand-placed grid arrangements: (a) a chain of three zero arcs lengthening away from a critical node whose far arc is the most crowded folds entirely onto the critical node, each pick the shortest live zero arc, each of the four hanging arcs re-routed exactly once; (b) of two collapsible zero arcs the one-edge one is chosen over a three-edge one whose moving node carries more arcs; (c) a zero arc re-embedded along a longer detour is re-ranked behind the other. DoD 6(a) was written for survivor-inward; since order2 lost, (a) tests the landed order on a chain where shortest-first yields the inward fold. All three fail when the selection is temporarily switched back to master's most-contended rule (checked, then restored). Full mvn test: 321 run, 0 failures, 0 errors. Final code re-swept (tmp/sweep-final.txt): botijo 20120, elk 11743, hand 7104 splits, identical to order1.

Outcome: order1 (shortest zero arc first) lands, the only order, no knob. Why: it cuts total splits vs master by 97% on botijo (696628 -> 20120) and 95% on elk (223739 -> 11743), worst single route from 150045 to 36 on botijo, contract 4.8 s -> ~1.3 s on botijo; order2 (survivor-inward) is about 2x worse than order1 on every model (botijo 42009, elk 26797), because forcing the survivor as the target drags the neighbour's whole fan onto it even when the neighbour is the busier node, while order1 keeps movingEndpoint's lower-degree choice. Bonus: block (figure_8, bias -1) now loads (PATCH-118's arc-178 fold-back does not occur), buddha loads in 37 s and feline in 22 s under 60 s; fandisk still fails in the embedding before the contraction. Unknown 1 (union-find vs local rule): not needed for the landed order; by reasoning, a local rule 'prefer zero arcs touching a critical node or one that already absorbed a collapse, else shortest' reproduces survivor-inward per cluster, since a second seed can only start once every seeded cluster is exhausted; the only difference is the survivor of a cluster without a critical node (the first shortest arc's survivor rather than a chosen node). Not implemented or measured. Unknown 2: survivor choice without a critical node moves splits by under 1% (lowest id vs node on an original copy vertex), and EmbeddedNode.vertexId is always -1 on ArcNetwork nodes, so 'already on a mesh vertex' must be read as copyVertex < topology.originalVertexBound. wt done passed: build, launch entry 'PATCH-120: quad-layout' (botijo) run headless, screenshots tmp/patch-120-botijo-quad-layout.png and tmp/patch-120-launch.png, ticket marked REVIEW.
